subject: Quarter-close: recap + next steps (Redwood x Quantum Health)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, Jul 21, 2026 at 14:12 PDT
Subject: Quarter-close: recap + next steps (Redwood x Quantum Health)

Hi Lena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum before quarter close:

- Discovery notes:
  • Primary objective: reduce per-call transcription latency and lower token costs for downstream analytics.
  • Key constraint: PHI-sensitive pipelines; must confirm data residency and SOC 2 artifacts.
  • Success metric: 30% reduction in inference cost per month or <150ms 95th-percentile serving for top paths.

- Proposed pilot:
  1) 4-week sandbox on our Dedicated tier (1-GPU equivalent) limited to a subset of 3 high-volume flows.
  2) Warm-start: we’ll onboard one model variant we benchmarked, provide prefix caching config and split traffic for evaluation.
  3) Measurement: weekly token-cost and latency dashboards + one regression eval.

- Asks from your side to get started:
  • Confirmation that procurement can approve a pilot up to $12k (monthly equivalent) or direction on POs/terms.
  • SOC2 summary and data residency checklist (we can deliver SOC2 summary and a network architecture diagram).
  • A point person from procurement to complete the vendor intake form.

I attached a short pilot proposal (QH-pilot-proposal.pdf) and SOC2 summary (SOC2-Summary.pdf) for procurement. If you’re still aiming for an end-of-quarter decision, would you confirm whether budget/approval timelines are still on track or likely to slip into next quarter?

If helpful, I can set a 20-min alignment with procurement + engineering this week (open windows: Fri 10–12 PT).

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Jul 27, 2026 at 09:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Quarter-close: recap + next steps (Redwood x Quantum Health)

Hi Lena — just bumping this in case it got buried. We want to make sure the pilot proposal and SOC2 summary reached the right people. Two quick options to keep things moving if timeline is tight:

1) Kick off a limited verification pilot (no PO) — Redwood covers the first two weeks of infra while procurement completes intake.
2) Schedule a 20-min call with procurement + engineering to confirm the minimal info they need to sign off.

If priority has shifted given quarter-close, totally understand — a quick note on timing (now vs. next quarter) will help us tailor the proposal and internal resource commitments.

Thanks — I’ll keep Friday morning open for a quick sync if that helps.

—
Soojin
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@quantumhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Caldwell <mark.caldwell@quantumhealth.com>, procurement@quantumhealth.com
Date: Thu, Jul 29, 2026 at 16:40 PDT
Subject: Re: Quarter-close: recap + next steps (Redwood x Quantum Health)

Soojin — thanks for the follow up and for the materials. Quick update from our side:

- Budget: senior leadership is doing a late re-prioritization for Q3 and we may not have a capital allocation available before the quarter closes. There is a realistic chance this moves to early Q4 unless we can show an immediate low-risk pilot cost that procurement can approve quickly.
- Compliance: procurement asked for a concise SOC2 artifact and network/data residency confirmation. They requested the one-pager SOC2-Summary.pdf and an architecture note.
- Procurement: I’ve looped in Mark (cc) and procurement@quantumhealth.com to pick up the vendor intake. They requested the vendor template (attached) and a single-point estimate of first-month spend.

Can Redwood share: a one-page estimate showing first-month cost for the pared-down pilot (2 flows, 1 model variant) and a short network diagram describing where logs/outputs land? If you can get that to Mark/procurement by EOD Monday, we’ll prioritize the intake to see if it can be fast-tracked.

If the intake can’t clear before quarter-end, we’ll likely revisit in early Q4. Apologies for the noise — appreciate the flexibility.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Product Partner, Quantum Health

[Attachment: procurement-template.pdf (fillable pdf)]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quarter-close: recap + next steps (Redwood x Quantum Health)

Hi Mark / procurement team — thanks for jumping in and Lena for the intro. I’m attaching a concise one-page estimate and a single-slide architecture summary (see links below). Quick summary here:

- Pilot scope: 2 production flows, single model variant, Dedicated sandbox with automatic prefix caching.
- Estimated first-month spend: $4,600 (infrastructure + support) — this assumes Redwood covers the onboarding hours and we bill starting at the verified pilot activation.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 one-pager and architecture slide attached (SOC2-Summary.pdf). We can provide a longer artifact package and a short redacted SOC2 report under an NDA if needed.

Proposed next step: 20-min call to approve vendor intake and lock the pilot window. I’m available today 11:00–12:00 PT or Monday 09:00–11:00 PT. If procurement prefers, I can also drop the formal vendor answers directly into your intake template.

Links / attachments:
- One-page estimate: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cQH-proposal
- SOC2 summary: https://app.redwood.ai/security/soc2-summary
- Procurement template completed (draft): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1procurement-draft

Looking forward to working with you and thanks again for trying to fast-track.

Best —
